source_row.extraction_instructions: Drupal site on the same platform/theme as RCoA. Listing at /events with a 0-INDEXED pager (?page=0 is page one, ?page=1 is page two; ?page=2 is empty) - 13 events across 2 pages on 2026-09-26. Cards are .l-listing-grid__item: link /events/<slug>, title, subtitle = format, category, summary, and a <time> whose text is a HUMAN date range ('25 March to 26 November 2026', '7 to 16 September 2026') - the datetime attribute repeats that text instead of an ISO stamp, so it must be parsed. Detail pages carry a .c-details-sidebar__details 'Key details' block keyed by .c-details-sidebar__highlight labels (Date / Location / Availability / CPD credits) and all tabs are server-rendered in the DOM (hidden with CSS, not lazy-loaded), so one fetch yields Overview, Programme, Pricing and any Abstract Competition panel; tab button -> panel via aria-controls. Fee tables sit in the Pricing panel with a '<Section> | Price' header row. CLOUDFLARE GOTCHA: browser.py's navigate() ALT_PROFILE switch clears FICM for exactly ONE page load per session; every later navigate() in the same session is re-challenged and never resolves. The extractor therefore fetches each page in a BRAND-NEW ALT_PROFILE context (browser.new_context(**ALT_PROFILE)), which clears in 0.4-0.8 s every time, and extract_detail() re-fetches when the page it is handed is the challenge.

registry_comment: FICM - Drupal /events, 0-indexed pager; Cloudflare needs a fresh browser context per page load (see docstring)

probe_results.notes: 13 events are listed across pages 0 and 1; 11 are upcoming. The 2 dropped had already finished: leeds-acute-intensive-care-conference-lactic (24-25 Sep 2026) and essential-radiology-for-icu-and-anaesthesia-1 (7-16 Sep 2026) - the FICM view itself still lists events a day or two past, so the end-date filter is doing real work. 'with_pricing 7' is full coverage of what FICM publishes: the 4 without fees genuinely show none on the page. 'shells_forced_fallback' is a second identical full run, not --force-fallback, which is meaningless here (the extractor is browser-first by design and never uses httpx). Specialty is 'Intensive Care Medicine' on 10 events and 'Critical Care Medicine' on 1. The single event with neither city nor venue is famusfusic, whose Key-details line is literally 'Location: In person,'.

concerns: browser.py's ALT_PROFILE switch clears FICM for exactly ONE page load per session, not for the session. Measured repeatedly on 2026-09-26: fresh BrowserController -> navigate('/events') gives the real 261 KB page, then navigate('?page=1'), navigate('/events/<slug>') and even navigate('/events') again all return the 403 'Just a moment' interstitial, which then never resolves (polled 40 s). The alternate context keeps its cf_clearance cookie and is re-challenged anyway. A BRAND-NEW context per load clears every time in 0.4-0.8 s, so this extractor opens one per page via browser.new_context(**ALT_PROFILE). Worth fixing centrally in browser.py - rotating the alt context per navigate would let FICM (and probably the other Cloudflare sources) use plain navigate() - but that is a shared file and other agents are in flight, so I did not touch it.

Because of the above, extract_detail() cannot use the page the scraper hands it: llm_agent navigates it first, and that navigation is load #2+ of the session. The extractor checks the page and re-fetches when it is the challenge. This costs one wasted navigation per event (~11/run) against a site that is actively refusing us. It is written to prefer the handed-in page automatically if browser.py is ever fixed, so no change here would be needed then.

FAMUS/FUSIC (/events/famusfusic) is classified event_type 'conference' but is really a recurring ultrasound course. Nothing on the FICM page says so - the title is just 'FAMUS/FUSIC', the slug has no keyword, the body is a bare list of dates plus an external boxcourses.co.uk link, and the category taxonomy ('External Event' / 'Education') is about audience, not type. Left as the default rather than guessing from a URL substring.
FAMUS/FUSIC also has venue_name and city None: its Key-details line is literally 'Location: In person,' with an empty venue. That is the site's own gap, not a parse failure.

The card and sidebar date strings are human text ('25 March to 26 November 2026') with no ISO stamp anywhere on the page, so dates depend on a month-name parser. It handles single dates, same-month ranges, cross-month ranges and year-spanning ranges (unit-tested against 11 strings including synthetic '1 December 2026 to 31 January 2027' and '20 December to 5 January 2027'). A non-English or abbreviated month ('Sept', '3rd Nov') would fail to parse and the event would be skipped with a log line rather than dated wrongly.

The city/venue splitter uses a hard-coded UK city list and an organisation-keyword list. It is correct on all 11 events, but an unlisted town in a comma-separated venue lands in city verbatim (acceptable) and an unlisted town on its own line lands in venue_name instead of city (minor).

FICM's own copy is inconsistent on intensivists-in-training-conference-2026: the structured venue says 'The Marriott, Manchester Piccadilly' while the Overview prose still reads 'Join us at the Mercure, Manchester'. The extractor takes the structured field for venue_name, but the LLM description repeats 'Mercure' from the prose. Only FICM can fix that.
max_pages_hint is 2 as of 2026-09-26; the extractor walks up to MAX_PAGES=6 and stops on the first page that yields no new events, so growth is handled without a config change.

Politeness: the full test cycle used roughly 60 page loads to ficm.ac.uk in total across all probing and three harness runs, sequential and single-browser. A production run costs 2 listing loads + 11 detail loads (plus the 11 wasted navigates noted above).
